text:
Priya Nair: quick heads-up from this morning's hotstart flake — worker stalled decoding a safetensors file that arrived gzipped without an index.
Ben Ortiz: saw that. stacktrace shows stream decoder waiting on frame boundary that never arrived.
Hector Morales: proxy returned 200 with `content-encoding: gzip` on the GET, but our stream path ignored `content-encoding` in one branch.
Rina Sato: ouch. short-term fix idea: loader should do a tiny 0-511 range probe and inspect magic bytes for compressed vs plain safetensors before deciding streaming path.
Priya Nair: range probe is fine but we need to be careful about double-request cost at scale. QPS at hotstart can be high.
Ben Ortiz: agree. add a per-host in-memory probe cache keyed by (url, etag|last-mod), TTL 45s, so we dedupe probes across concurrent hotstarts.
Hector Morales: also add a fast heuristic: if content-length is present and < 1_000_000 and no content-encoding header, prefer index-first only if index exists; otherwise allow small direct stream.
Rina Sato: proposal: decision tiers -> (A) cached probe result, (B) HEAD-probe header `x-rw-format` if present, (C) small-range GET peek, (D) conservative index-first.
Priya Nair: +1. For third-party registries that don't set headers, loader falls back to (B)->(C)->(D). Streaming must be opt-in via model manifest flag to avoid surprises.
Ben Ortiz: telemetry plan: emit probe.method=head|range|cache, probe.result=sf|sf+gz|tar|unknown, load.path=stream|index, and probe.latency_ms.
Hector Morales: runbook edits: how to force index-first per-model, how to toggle local probe cache size, how to interpret probe.latency spike alerts.
Rina Sato: safety note: when range probe returns truncated or inconsistent headers, loader should abort streaming immediately and fallback; don't let decoder hang for full request timeout.
Priya Nair: agreed. add a short decode deadline (e.g., 500ms) on initial stream before fallback. log a clear diagnostic with `probe=none->fallback` so ops can triage.
Ben Ortiz: I'll sketch the loader patch with cache and tiered probe. Hector can own the edge/registry guidance for `x-rw-format` header.
Hector Morales: happy to own edge docs. I'll propose header enum: `sf`, `sf+gz`, `tgz`, `tar`, `bin` and semantics (index-first preferred for `sf`, stream-only if `sf+gz` and size small).
Rina Sato: test matrix: unit tests for magic-byte detection, integration against gzipped safetensors served via nginx, load test to measure extra HEAD/range QPS with cache on/off.
infra-bot: created ISSUE-ML-1402: "loader tiered probe + host-level probe cache" assigned to Ben Ortiz, Hector Morales, Rina Sato. ETA: 2 sprints.
Priya Nair: canary plan: 1% Dedicated hotstarts -> monitor hotstart-latency, OOM spikes, probe.latency and probe.method distribution.
Ben Ortiz: note: document compatibility: older model stores may not have etag/last-mod; cache key should fall back to URL only then TTL shorter (15s).
Hector Morales: also add a debug endpoint on loader to dump cache entries and last probe timestamp for live triage.
Rina Sato: I'll add runbook steps for dumping cache and forcing re-probe.
Priya Nair: thanks team. I'll follow up with a short RFC PR with interface sketches and the probe header proto. :thumbsup:
